concept.name: Gap-and-go strategy
concept.definition: A day-trading momentum strategy that buys (or shorts) a stock that gaps at the open on high volume and continues trending in the gap direction without a meaningful pullback, entering on continuation beyond the opening range. It is a named practitioner setup with no canonical source.
concept.intuition: A high-volume gap means overnight information repriced the stock and trapped the other side; if price never looks back, the trapped traders' exits and momentum chasers feed a one-way move you ride with tight invalidation.
concept.mechanics: Screen for gaps with elevated premarket and opening volume; enter on the break of the opening range in the gap direction, place the stop at the prior session's close or the gap's far edge, and trail the exit with a trend line or the most recent swing low.
concept.failure_modes: The setup's evil twin is the gap fade: gaps that stall and fill trap momentum entries at the day's extreme, and wide opening spreads plus slippage make realized entries far worse than chart-based backtests suggest.
concept.misconceptions: That the gap direction is itself the signal; practitioners require volume confirmation and continuation structure - many gaps fill, and trading every gap is an exercise in chasing.
concept.example: A stock gaps up 8% on earnings with triple normal opening volume; the trader buys the break of the first 5-minute high, stops below the prior close, and exits when the rising trend line from the open is breached near midday.
